title: AB2883 (2021-2022): Firearms.

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk dataset (gun-policy Stage 5 LegiScan check, California); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official leginfo.legislature.ca.gov text (Amended 2022-04-28, via LegiScan getBillText)
provenance.note: Amended in Assembly 2022-04-28 (no floor vote; last version). This amendment struck the Government Code 53071 section (local liability-insurance ordinances not preempted); it is not in the version read.

operative_text:
Section 31640 (Penal Code): (e) (2) The department shall, no less frequently than once annually, update the internet website referenced in subdivision (d) to reflect current laws and regulations.
Section 34375 (Penal Code): (a) Commencing on July 1, 2023, upon the request of the City of San Jose, after enacting any code or ordinance imposing any requirement on the owners of firearms within the City of San Jose, the department shall mail a notification to each firearm owner of record within that jurisdiction to inform the owner of the new code or ordinance, any new requirements imposed upon the firearm owner, and any other information that may be helpful to the firearm owner in complying with the code or ordinance.
Section 34375 (Penal Code): (d) The City of San Jose shall be liable to the department for any costs incurred by the department for the processing and mailing of notifications to firearm owners.
Section 34375 (Penal Code): (f) The department shall not provide any personally identifying information to the City of San Jose regarding any firearm owner notified pursuant to this section.
Section 34377 (Penal Code): This chapter shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2030, and as of that date is repealed.
